hints.title: Matching Schools With Passing Exam Scores
hints.text: A score satisfies a school requirement if student_count is less than or equal to the school capacity.

hints.title: Choosing the Minimum Valid Score
hints.text: Left join Schools with Exam on student_count <= capacity. For each school, aggregate the minimum score among qualifying options.

hints.title: Fallback for Unreachable Capacities
hints.text: If no score has student_count <= capacity, return -1 using coalesce or ifnull.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT
    s.school_id,
    IFNULL(MIN(e.score), -1) AS score
FROM Schools s
LEFT JOIN Exam e
    ON e.student_count <= s.capacity
GROUP BY s.school_id;
```

complexity.time: O(S * E) for theta-join on capacity
complexity.space: O(S) space for grouped school cutoffs
variables: S: number of schools in Schools table
E: number of score tiers in Exam table
complexity.notes: Theta-join on student_count <= capacity with MIN aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: An inner join discards schools with small capacities where no exam score fits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: LEFT JOIN with IFNULL correctly assigns -1 when no valid score exists.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should choose MIN(score) and default null results to -1.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_cutoff_score(schools: pd.DataFrame, exam: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    m = pd.merge(schools, exam, how='cross')
    qual = m[m['student_count'] <= m['capacity']]
    if qual.empty:
        schools['score'] = -1
        return schools[['school_id', 'score']]
    grouped = qual.groupby('school_id')['score'].min().reset_index()
    res = pd.merge(schools[['school_id']], grouped, on='school_id', how='left')
    res['score'] = res['score'].fillna(-1).astype(int)
    return res
solutions.approach: Cross merge with capacity filtering in pandas
